claim: An AI growth engineer and an AI product engineer are not the same job: same tools, different scoreboard. The growth engineer is scored on the business number, the product engineer on the feature itself, and the title only tells you which number you are accountable for.
why_this_claim: It is the longform's own locked thesis (F2) answering the longform's own locked hook question (F1), proven by difference number one (the only one of the three differences whose two sides are each said in a single sentence) and closed by the CH5 payoff line that the screenplay wrote as the video's bookend. It needs no receipt, no chart, no diagram, no company name and no number to stand up cold, so it survives without the other three minutes. It is also the one claim whose proof sits on the panel-free FACE windows (F1, F2, F6) plus covers that survive a centre crop (BR-1, IMG-1, IMG-5), which is what this 16:9-sourced mode can frame; the clock and the bias each depend on a diagram, a chart or a side-panel face line.

assembled_read: 30.9 s delivered (27.9 s of spans + 3 s outro). So what are the differences between an AI growth engineer and an AI product engineer? They're not the same job, same tools, different scoreboard. Difference number one, the scoreboard, the growth engineer is scored on the business number, the signups, conversion, retention, and revenue. The product engineer is scored on the feature itself. And in my experience, a founding AI engineer ends up being both. Either way you're an AI engineer. The title just tells you which number you're accountable for.
